stories.title: How AI is being used to track art stolen by the Nazis
stories.summary: As momentum builds to recover artworks stolen during World War Two by the Nazis, researchers have created an AI chatbot that aims to trace the ownership and location history of works of art.

stories.title: Nearly 30 years after Tupac's death, the trial over his murder will finally begin
stories.summary: For decades the mystery of who killed Tupac Shakur plagued the public. In 2023, police charged Duane Davis, also known as "Keefe D," with organizing Shakur's murder. The trial begins Monday.

stories.title: 'Not a drop': Anger grows as Puerto Rico begins rationing water
stories.summary: Puerto Rico's government began cutting water service to people's homes this week, amid a severe drought that's exposing major weaknesses in the island's water delivery infrastructure.

stories.title: How a delivery driver and poet won one of China's highest honors in literature
stories.summary: Wang Jibing, a writer and delivery driver, has won one of China's most prestigious award for poetry. Professor Eileen Cheng-yin Chow of Duke University explains why his work has had such huge impact.

stories.title: National Guard deployment in D.C. approaches one year
stories.summary: President Trump's deployment of the National Guard will hit the one year mark next week. The presence of armed, uniformed troops on the street has become increasingly normalized in the capital.

stories.title: Meet the man circumnavigating the Arctic Ocean, alone
stories.summary: Matt Rutherford is sailing 10,000 nautical miles, through ice floes and gales, to try and accomplish a world first. He spoke with NPR from the cabin of his boat.
